title: Aero: Adaptive Query Processing of ML Queries
note: Adaptive query processing for ML/UDF queries in an ML-centric DBMS; single GPU

title: Heimdall: Optimizing Storage I/O Admission with Extensive Machine Learning Pipeline
note: Learned I/O admission policy with a full ML pipeline; the paper states it is ready for user-level deployment and the evaluation is trace replay with a 28 KB model. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - the in-kernel and distributed deployment variants need root, so the project must stay with the user-level replay path

title: GeneralSparse: Bridging the Gap in SpMM for Pruned Large Language Model Inference on GPUs
note: SpMM kernel generator for pruned LLM inference; evaluated single-GPU on A100 (Ampere, CUDA 12.1) which matches the A5000. Concern: 7B-class models in FP16 fit but larger ones need scale-down

title: VEGA: An Active-tuning Learned Index with Group-Wise Learning Granularity
note: Learned index with online model building under a memory budget; user space

title: Sieve: A Learned Data-Skipping Index for Data Analytics
note: Learned data-skipping index for analytics; single-node build, compares against Cuckoo-Index style baselines

title: Jenga: Effective Memory Management for Serving LLM with Heterogeneity
note: An attention-property-aware KV allocator implemented inside vLLM; single-GPU memory-utilization and throughput claims are directly measurable here, and the allocation policy is easy to perturb for an improvement hypothesis. Concerns - several evaluated models (large MoE and multimodal) exceed 24 GB, so the model set must be scaled down; upstream vLLM has moved on, so the AE snapshot may need pinning.

title: LOGER: A Learned Optimizer towards Generating Efficient and Robust Query Execution Plans
note: Learned query optimizer generating robust plans on PostgreSQL; GPU-optional training, single node

title: Improving Multiresource Job Scheduling with Markovian Service Rate Policies
note: Multiresource job scheduling policy class evaluated by trace-driven simulation on the Google Borg trace; C++ simulator, user space, no cluster needed. Concern: the paper's core contribution is queueing-theoretic (throughput optimality, response-time bounds) and the simulator is a supporting artifact, so an "improvement" project would be partly analytical; the Borg trace download is large and must be budgeted against ~257 GB free.

title: HybridTier: an Adaptive and Lightweight CXL-Memory Tiering System
note: Lightweight user-space memory-tiering policy with probabilistic hotness tracking; concern: the slow tier is a real CXL device in the paper, so on this machine it must be emulated (e.g. with a slower backing store or cgroup limits) since there is only one NUMA node

title: Amanda: Unified Instrumentation Framework for Deep Neural Networks
note: User-space operator-level instrumentation layer over PyTorch/TensorFlow; pure Python/C++ extension, single GPU is enough. Easy to extend with new instrumentation tools.

title: Learned Offline Query Planning via Bayesian Optimization
note: Offline learned query planner using Bayesian optimization on PostgreSQL

title: Morph: Efficient File-Lifetime Redundancy Management for Cluster File Systems
note: Redundancy-transcoding policy for cluster file systems, evaluated largely by trace-driven simulation over Google/production file-lifetime traces - exactly the simulation route env.md permits. Java artifact, user space. Concern: the HDFS prototype half of the evaluation wants a multi-node cluster; the project would have to stay on the simulator and single-node coding microbenchmarks.

title: EXIST: Enabling Extremely Efficient Intra-Service Tracing Observability in Datacenters
note: Per-mille-overhead intra-service (application-level) tracing - user-space instrumentation and sampling; concern: may rely on hardware tracing support and no official repo was found

title: SSCard: Substring Cardinality Estimation using Suffix Tree-Guided Learned FM-Index
note: learned FM-index based substring cardinality estimator - learned component inside a query optimizer - single-node CPU artifact

title: EINNET: Optimizing Tensor Programs with Derivation-Based Transformations
note: Derivation-based tensor program optimizer; evaluated on single V100 and A100 GPUs, so an A5000 is a valid scaled-down target. Code is explicitly released in the abstract and actively maintained. Concern: reported speedups are hardware-specific, so a reproduction will produce different absolute numbers on Ampere consumer-class silicon. AE artifact: https://github.com/zhengly123/OSDI23-EinNet-AE .

title: Viper: A Fast Snapshot Isolation Checker
note: Offline black-box checker over recorded transaction histories - a single-machine C++/SAT-solver pipeline with a companion ViperBench workload repo (figshare artifact also released). Performance of the BC-polygraph encoding and solver is exactly the kind of thing a 10-week improvement project can attack.

title: Efficient Exposure of Partial Failure Bugs in Distributed Systems with Inferred Abstract States
note: Fault-injection testing framework using Soot-based static analysis of JVM bytecode and inferred abstract states; the six targets (ZooKeeper, Kafka, HDFS, HBase, Cassandra, Flink) all run as local user-space JVM processes. Concerns: Java toolchain must be installed via conda; running small local clusters is RAM and disk heavy but fits; some fault types used in related work rely on tc (root-only) - FUSE-based faults are available.

title: Glign: Taming Misaligned Graph Traversals in Concurrent Graph Processing
note: Single-machine concurrent graph-processing runtime - CPU only user space  Zenodo artifact  alignment heuristics are an obvious improvement target

title: A Logically Disaggregated Cache for Replicated Storage Systems
note: Disaggregating the embedded caches of storage replicas into one logical cache - artifact implements LDC in a key-value store, so replicas can be run as several processes here. Concern: cross-replica network effects are lost on a single host

title: Hector: An Efficient Programming and Compilation Framework for Implementing Relational Graph Neural Networks in GPU Architectures
note: Two-level IR and CUDA code generator for relational GNNs; single-GPU evaluation against DGL/PyG on OGB heterogeneous graphs.

title: SilvanForge: A Schedule-Guided Retargetable Compiler for Decision Tree Inference
note: An ML compiler (MLIR/LLVM-based) that autoschedules decision-tree inference for both CPU and a single GPU - the paper's own evaluation platform is one multicore CPU plus one NVIDIA GPU, matching this machine almost exactly. Concern: needs a user-space LLVM/MLIR toolchain built from source (clang is not installed), which is a real but tractable setup cost. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/asprasad/treebeard/tree/silvanforge .

title: DAHA: Accelerating GNN Training with Data and Hardware Aware Execution Planning
note: cost-model-driven execution planning and pipelining for GNN training on CPU-GPU

title: Optimal Kernel Orchestration for Tensor Programs with Korch
note: Operator fission plus ILP-based kernel orchestration for DNN inference; evaluated on single V100/A100 GPUs, so an A5000 run is a direct scale-down.

title: Minuet: Accelerating 3D Sparse Convolutions on GPUs
note: Single-GPU sparse-convolution engine (segmented sort + binary search instead of hash tables, tile autotuning). Runs on one commodity GPU; point-cloud datasets are small. Concern - autotuned tile sizes were tuned for A100/V100 class GPUs so numbers will shift on an RTX A5000 with CUDA 11.8; that shift is itself a plausible improvement angle

title: Write-Aware Timestamp Tracking: Effective and Efficient Page Replacement for Modern Hardware
note: Write-aware timestamp tracking page-replacement policy in a buffer manager; single-node NVMe, pure user-space C++. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/leanstore/leanstore/tree/WATT .

title: TreeLine: An Update-In-Place Key-Value Store for Modern Storage
note: Single-node update-in-place KV store on NVMe as a RocksDB alternative; C++ user-space build, io_uring/O_DIRECT only, dataset fits the 257 GB free space

title: InferF: Declarative Factorization of AI/ML Inferences over Joins
note: factorization of ML inference over joins implemented in Velox - an inference runtime/compiler artifact that runs on CPU

title: Identifying and Analyzing Pitfalls in GNN Systems
note: Reproduction-oriented analysis of accuracy and memory pitfalls in GNN systems, explicitly framed around single-GPU systems and run on one A100 40 GB. Concern: the paper only points at the lab GitHub org rather than a named GraphPy repo, so the exact artifact needs identification

title: Toppings: CPU-Assisted, Rank-Aware Adapter Serving for LLM Inference
note: CPU-assisted rank-aware LoRA adapter serving built on LightLLM; Llama2-7B is served on a single GPU and the CPU-assist path suits a 16-core/32-thread host. Concern: no artifact URL appears in the paper although the ATC25 AE page awarded Available/Functional/Reproduced - repo not found by search

title: SimAI: Unifying Architecture Design and Performance Tuning for Large-Scale LLM Training
note: Official Alibaba artifact (URL printed in the paper). The analytical and ns-3-backed simulation modes are CPU-only user-space builds, so "simulate a 1k-GPU cluster" costs no GPUs; accuracy-vs-speed of the simulator is a testable hypothesis. Concerns: the SimAI-Physical mode needs a real GPU/RDMA cluster and must be skipped; the build pulls a large ns-3/MPI toolchain that has to be installed under $HOME.

title: FreeRide: Harvesting Bubbles in Pipeline Parallelism
note: Middleware that detects idle pipeline-parallel bubbles and schedules generic GPU side tasks into them with MPS-based resource capping. Concern: evaluated on 4x RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB) plus a second server; pipeline parallelism needs >=2 stages, so a single-GPU scale-down means emulating 2 stages as separate processes on the one A5000 with a small model (nanoGPT-class). Concern: the side-task isolation path uses Docker, which is not installed and would need replacing by cgroup v2 + MPS (both usable unprivileged here). Core mechanism itself is per-GPU and user space.

title: Lero: A Learning-to-Rank Query Optimizer
note: Learning-to-rank query optimizer for PostgreSQL; PostgreSQL builds from source into $HOME, model training is small enough for one GPU or CPU

title: Mitigating the Impedance Mismatch between Prediction Query Execution and Database Engine
note: Prediction-aware operator with inference context reuse and batching inside a DB engine; single GPU

title: PipeThreader: Software-Defined Pipelining for Efficient DNN Execution
note: DNN compiler with software-defined pipelining, open-sourced inside TileLang; single-GPU by construction (FlashAttention, Mamba2 kernels). Concerns: the headline motivation is the Hopper Tensor Memory Accelerator, which Ampere lacks - the A5000 can only exercise the TensorCore/async-copy subset; also note the repo is the whole TileLang project, so the PipeThreader-specific code must be located within it.

title: Enjima: A Resource-Adaptive Stream Processing System
note: scale-up stream processing engine with its own user-space memory management and operator scheduler - squarely a user-space systems artifact for one machine

title: Building Verified Neural Networks for Computer Systems with Ouroboros
note: Training-verification loop that produces neural networks with provable safety properties for systems tasks such as learned indexes and caching - artifact states no specific hardware is required with a 1 to 5 hour experiment time - concern - depends on Julia plus NeuralVerification.jl and the verification step is CPU-heavy

title: GFS: A Preemption-aware Scheduling Framework for GPU Clusters with Predictive Spot Instance Management
note: Preemption-aware GPU-cluster scheduler with demand forecasting; policy work that can be studied trace-driven or in simulation. Concern: repo has no README yet and the paper evaluates a real cluster

title: Optimal Scheduling Algorithms for LLM Inference: Theory and Practice
note: SLO-aware prefill/decode scheduler with a throughput-optimality proof and a practical scheduler. Already evaluated with Mistral-7B on a single 48 GB RTX 6000 Ada - the closest of any paper here to the target machine. Concern: 7B in FP16 plus KV cache is tight in 24 GB, so shorter contexts or a quantized model

title: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
note: Prefix-cache admission and eviction policy for hybrid LLMs - the artifact is a trace-driven Python simulator so the whole evaluation runs on CPU, with the GPU only needed for optional end-to-end checks - ideal project target

title: MariusGNN: Resource-Efficient Out-of-Core Training of Graph Neural Networks
note: Explicitly a single-machine single-GPU out-of-core GNN training system whose whole thesis is that one GPU plus SSD beats multi-GPU baselines. Mature open-source repo with the EuroSys'23 artifact tag. Concern - the largest evaluated graphs need hundreds of GB of disk; 257 GB free means smaller graphs only.

title: IMPRESS: An Importance-Informed Multi-Tier Prefix KV Storage System for Large Language Model Inference
note: Importance-informed prefix-KV identification plus multi-tier (DRAM/SSD) KV cache placement to cut TTFT - entirely user-space, single GPU, SSD-bound, a natural fit for the machine. Concerns - no standalone FAST '25 artifact; the released repo is HyperInfer, the same authors' journal extension, which states it keeps the original FlexGen/H2O-based prototype. Paper uses OPT-6.7B/13B/30B; only 6.7B fits 24 GB in FP16 without offload, though offloading is central to the design.

title: TensorDex: A Compact, Tensor-Centric Storage System for Modern AI Models
note: TStore - tensor-level delta compression for model hubs, with learned pairwise compressibility prediction instead of lineage metadata. CPU plus disk workload, no GPU needed, and 257 GB free on /home is enough for a scaled-down model corpus. Concern: the paper studies petabyte-scale hubs so the corpus must be subsampled, and no artifact link appears in the preprint.

title: Making LSM-Tree-based Key-Value Store Practical and Efficient for Multi-Tenant Serverless Cloud Databases
note: LSM key-value store with I/O admission control and deferred compaction, built on RocksDB - storage-engine work - concern: the motivation is multi-tenant cloud over-subscription - no repo located

title: Mitigating Application Resource Overload with Targeted Task Cancellation
note: Atropos is a user-space overload-control framework integrated into MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch, Solr, Apache and etcd - all single-host, root-free workloads, and 16 cores / 125 GB is ample to reproduce the 16 overload scenarios. The culprit-scoring policy is a clean target for an improvement hypothesis. Concerns - per-request resource monitoring may want signals this machine restricts (no perf counters); cgroup v2 cpu/memory/pids are delegated, which should cover the resource-limiting side.

title: DBAIOps: A Reasoning LLM-Enhanced Database Operation and Maintenance System using Knowledge Graphs
note: Reasoning LLM plus knowledge graph system for database anomaly diagnosis and recovery; agent and knowledge base run in user space against a local DBMS

title: Fast and Efficient Model Serving Using Multi-GPUs with Direct-Host-Access
note: DL inference serving with model provisioning from host memory - BERT/RoBERTa/GPT-2 class models fit in 24 GB. Best-artifact award, libTorch-based, no kernel or hypervisor dependency. Concern - the second of the two techniques (parallel model transmission across several GPUs) cannot be reproduced on one GPU; only the direct-host-access half scales down.

title: Algorithmic Complexity Attacks on Dynamic Learned Indexes
note: complexity attacks on the ALEX dynamic learned index; pure user-space C++ experiments

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention (vLLM)
note: KV-cache paging plus continuous batching; the canonical single-GPU LLM serving substrate. Runs entirely in user space on one CUDA GPU. Fits the A5000 with 7B FP16 models. Concerns - paper evaluates OPT-13B/66B/175B on multi-GPU A100 nodes so absolute numbers need scale-down to 7B-class; modern vLLM main branch has drifted far from the SOSP artifact (AE snapshot is https://github.com/sosp-ae-39/sosp-ae-astra) so pinning a version matters; recent wheels may want CUDA >12.2 which is a driver-535 risk

title: Don't Let AI Agents YOLO Your Files: Information and Control in Agent-Native Filesystems
note: YoloFS - an agent-native filesystem that stages mutations, snapshots, and gates accesses for AI coding agents. FUSE is usable unprivileged on this machine (/dev/fuse world-rw, setuid fusermount3). Code is explicitly open-sourced in the abstract. Concern: the evaluation drives real coding agents so it needs LLM API budget.

title: TTLs Matter: Efficient Cache Sizing with TTL-Aware Miss Ratio Curves and Working Set Sizes
note: Purely trace-driven MRC/WSS algorithms (TTL-aware SHARDS, TTL-aware HyperLogLog) - CPU and RAM only, no privileged access. 28 public cache traces with 113 billion accesses; disk space for the full trace set (~257 GB free) is the only real constraint

title: MiniMalloc: A Lightweight Memory Allocator for Hardware-Accelerated Machine Learning
note: Offline static memory allocator (2D packing solver) for ML accelerator buffers - single-threaded C++ CPU solver with open benchmarks  fully open source

title: Oasis: An Out-of-core Approximate Graph System via All-Distances Sketches
note: Single-machine out-of-core system that trades memory for SSD I/O when building and querying All-Distances Sketches; user-space C++ with an explicit memory-budget knob, which suits a 125 GiB / NVMe box well. Concerns - large graph inputs plus multi-times-graph-size sketches must fit in ~257 GB free, so the biggest datasets in the paper may need to be dropped.

title: QiMeng-Xpiler: Transcompiling Tensor Programs for Deep Learning Systems with a Neural-Symbolic Approach
note: LLM + symbolic-synthesis transcompiler; the toolchain itself is user-space Python and the CUDA target is testable on the A5000. Concern: three of the four evaluated back-ends (Intel AVX512-VNNI, AMD MI HIP, Cambricon BANG) do not exist on this AMD Zen3 + NVIDIA machine, so only a subset of the translation matrix can be reproduced; also needs an LLM API budget. Available + Functional, not Reproduced.

title: Camel: Efficient Compression of Floating-Point Time Series
note: Floating-point compression codec plus index; user-space library

title: Accurate and Ultra-Fast Launch-Time Validation of Idempotency for GPU Kernels
note: Launch-time validation of GPU kernel idempotency - user-space analysis on a single GPU, self-contained. No code found yet

title: Spain: Succinct Proofs for Numerical Computations
note: User-space prover/front-end toolchain with a clear, reproducible performance target (prover time and constraint count for float-heavy computations); most benchmarks need under 5 GB RAM. Concerns: the artifact is Docker-based (must be ported to conda/source) and the largest GPT-2 configuration needs ~270 GB RAM (we have 125 GiB) - stick to the small benchmarks

title: Efficient Lossless Compression of Scientific Floating-Point Data on CPUs and GPUs
note: Four new lossless floating-point compressors, pure user-space CPU and single-GPU code; SDRBench inputs are downloadable; ideal scale for the machine

title: PARD: Enhancing Goodput for Inference Pipeline via Proactive Request Dropping
note: Proactive request dropping to maximize goodput of multi-model inference pipelines - a scheduling policy that can be evaluated on one GPU or in simulation. No code found yet

title: xMem: A CPU-Based Approach for Accurate Estimation of GPU Memory in Deep Learning Training Workloads
note: The estimator itself runs CPU-only (dynamic analysis of allocator behaviour), so the expensive half of the pipeline needs no GPU at all; the single A5000 is only needed to collect ground-truth peak memory. Their 25-model suite is CNN/Transformer training, most of which fits in 24 GB at reduced batch size. Concern: a few of the 25 models may not fit in 24 GB, so the validation set will have to be trimmed; 5209 runs is a lot of wall-clock on one GPU and would need subsampling.

title: D-Bot: Database Diagnosis System using Large Language Models
note: LLM-based DBMS diagnosis agent; can run against a local PostgreSQL. Concern: needs an LLM endpoint

title: Learning to Optimize LSM-trees: Towards A Reinforcement Learning based Key-Value Store for Dynamic Workloads
note: RL-based tuning of LSM-tree compaction/configuration on top of RocksDB. Concern: no artifact found in GitHub search, repo unknown

title: DDB: Source-Level Interactive Debugging for Distributed Applications
note: Source-level interactive debugger for distributed applications - user-space tooling, no root needed. Evaluated against systems like LogCabin and Jepsen-style workloads that can be run as several processes on one host. Concern: no artifact URL in the preprint and distributed timeout behaviour may differ when everything is colocated.

title: DOT: Dynamic Knob Selection and Online Sampling for Automated Database Tuning
note: Knob importance pruning plus Bayesian optimization with no warm-up phase; runs against a local DBMS with sysbench and TPC-H

title: Divo: Learning a Stable and Effective Query Optimizer with a Diverse Workload
note: learned query optimizer trained on diverse generated workloads - learned system component - concern: RL training over 100k plans is compute-heavy but CPU-feasible - no repo located

title: Optimizing PyTorch Inference with LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
note: Comparative framework for LLM multi-agent PyTorch optimization on KernelBench, with code and a Zenodo archive. Concerns: reported speedups are H100 baselines that must be re-measured on Ampere, and agent search needs LLM API budget

title: Learning to Parallelize with OpenMP by Augmented Heterogeneous AST Representation
note: Learned detector for OpenMP-parallelizable loops using an augmented heterogeneous AST - CPU-only training and inference on a released dataset - concern - the contribution is a model plus dataset rather than a running system and only the OMP_Serial dataset is clearly released by the authors so the official model code is uncertain

title: Can Large Language Models Be Query Optimizer for Relational Databases?
note: LLM-based query optimizer on top of PostgreSQL with instruction tuning - learned system component - concern: fine-tuning an LLM on one 24 GB GPU needs scale-down - no repo located

title: GRF: A Global Range Filter for LSM-Trees with Shape Encoding
note: Global range filter for LSM-trees with shape encoding - direct RocksDB-level artifact. Concern: checked GitHub repo search and web search, no artifact link found

title: Rhyme Native: Efficient Code Generation for Structured and Semi-Structured Workloads
note: Code generation for a declarative query language covering both relational and nested JSON workloads including a corrected loop scheduler; compiler and runtime work in user space

title: HotHash: Hotness-Aware Consistent Hashing for Cloud Databases
note: hotness-aware consistent hashing for query scheduling and cache locality in cloud databases - a scheduling/load-balancing policy that can be studied by simulation or multiple local processes - concern: no repo located

title: RABIT: Efficient Range Queries with Bitmap Indexing
note: group-encoded, SIMD-accelerated compressed bitmap index with multi-version updates - compression and cache-conscious layout in user space - concern: it is a DBMS index rather than an OS-level artifact - no repo located

title: CEGS: Configuration Example Generalizing Synthesizer
note: A learned component (GNN querier + GNN classifier + LLM-driven synthesis) driving a systems-management task; Python artifact, GNNs train comfortably on one 24 GB GPU. Concerns: the README expects Docker for the Batfish verification service (Docker is not installed - Batfish would have to be built from source or replaced) and an OpenAI API key, which costs money; a local 7-8B model on the A5000 is a plausible but unvalidated substitute.

title: LEON: A New Framework for ML-Aided Query Optimization
note: ML-aided query optimization framework on PostgreSQL; single node, small models

title: tf.data service: A Case for Disaggregating ML Input Data Processing
note: Input-data pipelines are explicitly in scope; the system is open source inside TensorFlow (paper states so and cites the TensorFlow GitHub project). Dispatcher and workers are ordinary user-space processes that can all be co-located on the 16-core host with one A5000 to study input-bound training. Concern: the paper's headline results are Google-fleet-scale; only a single-node, multi-process scale-down is possible, and the released code is a production subsystem rather than a paper artifact.

title: Abacus: A Cost-Based Optimizer for Semantic Operator Systems
note: Cost-based optimizer for LLM-powered semantic operator pipelines released inside the Palimpzest system. Concern: optimization quality depends on LLM API cost and non-determinism

title: Libra: One-Shot Parameter Sensitivity Estimation for Transfer Learning in Database Performance Prediction
note: One-shot parameter sensitivity profiles for transferring performance models across contexts. Concern: the published study spans seven hardware environments so only the released measurement data can be reused here

title: How Much Can RocksDB Chew? Achieving Near-Zero Write Stalls with Sustainable RocksDB
note: Reframes RocksDB write stalls as a control problem and adds an online RL admission controller; single-node and directly reproducible on NVMe

title: Improving DNN Inference Throughput Using Practical, Per-Input Compute Adaptation
note: E3 splits and replicates blocks of early-exit models to keep batch size constant; a user-space serving-layer mechanism that can be exercised with one A5000 on BERT/GPT-2 class models. Concern: no artifact found - not in the SOSP 2024 AE results, and no repo on the authors' GitHub accounts (checked dywsjtu, MingyuGuan, ruipan, swapnilgandhi, anandpiyer) or the Georgia Tech NEXS project page. Marked unknown rather than out-no-code because the closely related Apparate artifact from the same group is public and E3 code may live unlinked.

title: Efficient Dynamic Indexing for Range Filtered Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: Dynamic range-filtered ANN index with linear space; single machine

title: MirrorKV: An Efficient Key-Value Store on Hybrid Cloud Storage with Balanced Performance of Compaction and Querying
note: LSM key-value store splitting hot/cold across fast and slow storage; can be emulated with NVMe plus a throttled/slow tier. Concern: checked GitHub and web search, no artifact found
